rv.q: She is hard as nails and sharp as tacks but Staunton·also lets us see her vulnerability: the fear of poverty and thwarted ambition that drive her. All this comes together in a show-stopping finale so near breaking point it is painful to watch, as, with both daughters gone, she is faced with the truth about herself.

But in situ at the Savoy, a more fitting venue for the fading vaudevillian world Rose seeks to conquer, not only does·Staunton display greater leather-lunged force in the showstopping numbers such as Everything's Coming Up Roses (sublime music, Jule Styne; razor-sharp lyrics, Stephen Sondheim).

For my money, she also gave the performance of 2014 in Good People at Hampstead and then later in the West End. Now here she is being more brilliant than ·ever and making us wonder why Gypsy (1959) hasn't been seen in London for-so long.
